title: NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own) — Renewal Billing and the Grace Period
content:
## Renewal billing and grace — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)

**Renewal bill.** Tidemark issues the renewal bill the tier's renewal notice period, in calendar days, before the term end, and also sends it to the mortgagee of record when the policy is mortgage-required and the tier sends the bill copy to the mortgagee. The renewal bill carries the rating engine's indicated full-risk premium for the coming term.

**Renewed term premium.** *Clause no longer in force:* "The risk premium booked for the renewed term is the lower of that indicated premium and the prior term's rated risk premium increased by the tier's annual risk premium increase cap, rounded to the cent; the ICC premium and Federal Policy Fee are the engine's figures for the coming term." This clause is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis. The Reserve Fund Assessment, HFIAA surcharge and any probation surcharge are booked as for new business.

**Payment by the term end.** When the full renewal premium is received on or before the term end the term is renewed on the same policy number with no break. When it is not, the policy enters renewal grace at the term end.

**Grace-period renewal.** A grace-period renewal is booked only when the full renewal premium is received no later than the tier's renewal grace period, in calendar days, after the policy term expires, counted by adding the days to the term end on the calendar, a receipt on the last grace day qualifying; the renewed term then starts on the prior term end with no break in coverage. A grace-period renewal is booked only on a policy whose status is renewal grace, and leaves it in force. The date read for the payment is the posted date of the payment on the premium account; the expiry read is the term end on the policy record.

**Losses in grace.** A loss that occurs during the grace period is covered only if the renewal premium is received inside the grace period.

**Lapse.** When the grace period ends unpaid the policy lapses with coverage ended at the term end; a payment received after that cannot renew the policy and is refunded, and coverage requires a new application subject to the waiting-period rule.

### The grace window at its boundary

| Full renewal premium received | Result |
|---|---|
| On or before the term end | Renewed on the same policy number, no break |
| After the term end, on or before the last grace day | Policy in renewal grace; grace-period renewal booked, new term starting on the prior term end, policy back in force |
| After the last grace day | Policy lapsed at the term end; payment refunded; a new application is needed |

*Hypothetical boundary (abstract dates).* With a grace period of a given number of days, the last grace day is found by adding that number of days to the term end on the calendar. A full renewal premium posted on that last grace day qualifies for a grace-period renewal; one posted on the next day does not, and is refunded.
